Speaking and Listening: Describing Pictu.title: Learning to Describe What You See

scenes.title: The Magic of Details
narration: Have you ever looked at a photo and wondered how to tell a story about it?
Describing helps us share our world with friends so they can see it too.
Let us learn how to paint a picture with our words.

scenes.title: Using Describing Words
narration: First, look for adjectives to describe colors, sizes, and shapes.
Instead of saying a dog, say a fluffy golden dog.
Use action verbs to explain what is happening in the scene.
The boy runs across the green park.

scenes.title: Describing a Market Scene
narration: Imagine we are at a busy vegetable market in Delhi.
I see bright red tomatoes and piles of fresh spinach.
A vendor is weighing crunchy carrots on his scale.
The market smells like spicy masala and fresh earth.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up Your Story
narration: Remember to use adjectives for appearance and verbs for actions.
Organize your thoughts to tell a clear and exciting story.
Think about it: What is one detail you can add to describe your favorite toy?

scenes.title: The Power of Clear Speech
narration: Have you ever tried to tell a story but felt your words got all tangled up?
Speaking clearly helps your friends understand your exciting ideas perfectly.
Let us learn how to pronounce words so everyone hears you loud and clear.

scenes.title: Focusing on Every Sound
narration: Pronunciation is just the way we say the sounds inside a word.
Try saying the word 'water' slowly, feeling the 't' sound at the middle.
Each letter has a job, and giving them time makes speech easy to follow.
Try exaggerating your mouth shapes to make sure every vowel is crisp.

scenes.title: Example Practice Session
narration: Look at these three words: cat, bat, and hat.
Notice how changing just the first letter makes a totally new sound.
Now say 'The cat wears a hat' very clearly to your friend.
By pausing between words, you give the listener time to catch every sound.

scenes.title: Recap and Try It Out
narration: Remember to speak slowly, shape your mouth, and practice your sounds daily.
Clear speaking makes you a confident leader in the classroom.
Think about it, what is one long word you find tricky to say today?

scenes.title: The Classroom Talk
narration: Have you ever tried talking with friends and everyone spoke at once?
That is like a noisy market, and no one hears the important ideas.
A group discussion is different because we take turns to share thoughts.

scenes.title: The Golden Rules
narration: First, always listen carefully while your friend is speaking.
Next, use kind words like I agree with you or That is interesting.
Finally, if you disagree, say I have a different opinion please.

scenes.title: A Discussion In Action
narration: Imagine Rohan, Priya, and Kabir are discussing their school garden project.
Rohan says, We should plant marigolds because they grow fast.
Priya listens and says, That is a great idea, but let us add roses too.
Kabir nods and says, I agree, let us make a list of seeds.

scenes.title: Wrap Up And Reflect
narration: Remember, good discussions need patience, listening, and polite words for everyone.
When we speak clearly and listen well, we solve problems together easily.
Think about it, how can you help someone who is shy join your group talk?

scenes.title: The Hook
narration: Have you ever stumbled over your words while telling a story to a friend?
Speaking smoothly is called fluency, and it makes you a great storyteller.
Let's learn how to speak with confidence and rhythm.

scenes.title: The Big Idea
narration: Fluency is not about speed; it is about reading or speaking naturally.
You should pause at periods and commas just like you take a breath.
Adding feeling to your voice helps listeners understand your excitement.

scenes.title: A Real Example
narration: Imagine telling your friend, Rohan, about a fun trip to Delhi.
Bad fluency sounds like: I went to Delhi and saw the Red Fort.
Good fluency sounds like: I went to Delhi, and I saw the Red Fort!
See how pausing after Delhi makes the sentence easier to follow?

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Remember, read slowly, pause at punctuation, and use your voice to show feeling.
Fluency turns simple words into a wonderful performance.
Think about it: Can you read a paragraph aloud today and pause at every comma?
